milestones.name: On the Mac, the moving 10,000-entity scene is held in a ray-tracing structure, rebuilt every frame at the poses that frame draws
milestones.quality_bar: A scene structure a shipped ray-traced renderer could shade from: every active entity present at the pose its frame draws it, nothing stale, and nothing at all for a scene that did not ask.

items.statement: A launch that names `ray-query` on this Mac gets a device with ray queries enabled, and the registry reports them. A launch that names nothing gets the device it gets today: no experimental feature and the same limits. An unknown name, and `ray-query` on an adapter that does not offer it, are each refused by name before a device is made.
items.ask: Do the Mac window, the capture runner and the test gate each take the request through the registry's one function, with the refusal decided from adapter facts and no test of platform, backend or adapter name?

items.statement: In a scene of entities on several meshes, with mirrored, scaled and inactive slots, a ray aimed through the middle of each active entity hits that entity, and a ray aimed where an inactive slot would stand, or past every entity, hits nothing. Each ray's answer is plain from how the scene was built, and none passes near an edge.
items.ask: Would a structure that held an inactive slot, lacked a mirrored one, or placed a scaled one at unit size fail this test?

items.statement: Through a scripted run of 10,000 entities with 1,500 movers, the instance list the scene structure is built from is the frame's own at every submitted frame: one instance for each active slot and none for an inactive one, with the mesh the slot draws and the matrix the vertex stage uses at that frame's presentation alpha, across entities that appear, disappear and change mesh. In each frame a ray aimed where a fast mover is drawn hits it, and a ray aimed where it was drawn the frame before misses it.
items.ask: Would a structure built from the committed pose in place of the interpolated one, or one frame late, fail this test?

items.statement: A device replacement rebuilds every mesh structure and the scene structure before the first frame that traces. A frame that is recorded and then discarded leaves the next frame's structure right. No frame traces a structure from another device generation.

A scene with no ray demand creates no structure, records no structure pass and changes no buffer's usage, on a device that enabled ray queries and on one that did not, and its submitted bytes are the ones it submits on main. On one device with ray queries enabled, a scene with no ray demand that is prepared beside one with it is unchanged in the same way.

The structure's cost is on record with the machine's load: resident bytes, the first build, and each frame's rebuild as CPU time and as GPU time, at 10,000 entities with none moving, with 1,500 movers and with every entity moving, and at the field's 100,513 instances. Each tripwire of the design's cost account that the record trips has its investigation beside it. No figure in the record decides this item.
No exact baseline moves: with no request, every registered image on the Mac's two recipes and in Chrome is the one on main.

milestones.name: The whole valley is in the ray-tracing structure, terrain and cooked meshes included, on screen or off, and an edited mesh is replaced there in the frame it changes on screen
milestones.quality_bar: The structure of a shipped ray-traced game's world: the terrain and every mesh in the scene, whether or not the camera sees it, with an edit showing in rays and on screen together. The traced view lines up with the drawn frame as a ray-tracing debug view does in a shipped engine.

items.statement: In the valley the traced view shows what the drawn frame shows: the terrain, every cooked mesh and the entities standing on them, each where it is drawn, with none missing, extra or out of place.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills of the traced view beside the drawn frame, at four views of the valley that between them show the terrain near and far and every cooked mesh, whole and as native-size crops where meshes meet the terrain.

items.statement: A contribution puts its geometry in the scene structure through one optional method of the contribution seam, offering each frame every opaque placement it holds in the scene, whether or not a view or a pass draws it. A contribution that offers nothing is unchanged, and `thrum-render` has gained no dependency on `thrum-asset-gpu`.
items.ask: Could the author of another contribution offer its opaque geometry from the seam's documentation alone: what to offer, when, and what the mask's two bits mean?

items.statement: When a cooked mesh that placements draw, and a cooked mesh row that entities draw, are each edited while the game runs, the structure changes in the publication's switch frame. A ray through a part only the new mesh has hits from that frame on and misses in every frame before it, and a ray through a part only the old mesh has does the reverse. A discarded switch frame is repeated with the same result, and a refused publication changes neither rays nor image.
items.ask: Is the frame in which the rays change shown to be the frame in which the drawn image changes, from the same run?

items.statement: Membership is decided before any view or pass culls. Every active entity and every placement the cooked contribution holds is an instance, with the shadow bit set exactly for what the scene declares a caster. A caster outside the camera's view and outside every Sun pass's volume is in the structure, and turning the camera changes no instance.
items.ask: Is the expected set taken from the scene's own records of what it holds and what casts, so that an instance list built from any pass's submitted draws would fail?

items.statement: In a scene with ray demand, every resident mesh's structure is built before the scene is ready, at first load and after a device replacement. While the game plays, a mesh structure is built only for an edit.

On one device with ray queries enabled, a cooked scene with no ray demand and one with it are prepared side by side. The first's cooked meshes have the buffer usages they have on main and no structure, and its submitted bytes are main's. The second's have the build usage and their structures. Each contribution learns the demand from its scene's surface before it makes a buffer.

The valley's structures are on record with the machine's load: resident bytes, the build time of each mesh structure against its triangle count, and the GPU time an edit's rebuild adds to its frame. Each tripwire of the design's cost account that the record trips has its investigation beside it. No figure in the record decides this item.
No exact baseline moves: with no request, every registered image on the Mac's two recipes and in Chrome is the one on main.

milestones.name: The Sun and lamps cast ray-traced shadows in the valley on the Mac: right at contact and at any distance, with hard edges
milestones.quality_bar: Hard ray-traced shadows as Cyberpunk 2077 shows its ray-traced Sun and local shadows before they are softened: no acne, no gap where a caster touches, no leak, and the same at one metre as at the far ridge.

items.statement: In scenes built so the answer is plain, the Sun visibility the scene's shader computes under `Traced` is that answer: a point under the middle of a slab is dark and a point well clear of it is lit, on terrain, on a prop and on a mover, with the Sun 1°, 10° and 45° up and overhead, and at a receiver beyond the cascades' reach. At 10 km and at 20 km from the scene's origin, a broad panel stands the design's supported separation in front of a wall, with the Sun beyond it: the wall behind the panel's middle is dark, and the wall beside the panel is lit.
items.ask: Is the value the operation the forward pass compiles, evaluated at the point on the receiving surface itself, so that a ray started beyond the panel would fail?

items.statement: In the populated valley, traced Sun shadows show no acne on a lit surface, no dark facets where a rounded body turns from the Sun, no gap and no leak where a prop or a balloon's basket meets what it stands on, and no shadow missing or out of place: at noon, at a low Sun and at dusk, near the camera and at the far ridge.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills at the route's stops at those three times with the method `Traced`, whole and as native-size crops of contact points, grazing slopes, balloons where they turn from the Sun and the far ridge, with the same stops under `Maps` beside them to show what differs.

items.statement: Shadows of the balloons and of everything else that moves stay under what casts them along the route at normal speed. In no frame is a shadow absent, doubled or a frame behind its caster.
items.inspect: A `realtime` sequence of the route with the method `Traced`, as consecutive frames at native size around three movers.

items.statement: With lamp shadows asked for, in scenes built so the answer is plain, a lamp's light at a surface point is cut where a body stands between them and not otherwise: with one lamp, with several that overlap, at a point in a cluster the lamp barely reaches, and with a body beyond the lamp, which casts nothing. A wall outside the camera's view and outside every Sun pass's volume keeps a lamp off the receiver behind it, and turning the camera changes nothing. At the quality value's default no lamp in range is unshadowed. Lowered, the lamps beyond it are unshadowed at that fragment and counted.
items.ask: Is the wall of the off-screen case outside both Sun pass volumes and the camera's view in the test as written, so that an instance list taken from any pass's draws would fail?

items.statement: At the valley's local-light stop at night, each lamp's shadows fall away from it and meet their casters at contact, and nothing behind a wall or a prop is lit by a lamp on its other side.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills at that stop with lamp shadows on and off, whole and as native-size crops around each lamp.

items.statement: `Auto` resolves to `Maps`. An explicit `Traced`, and a lamp-shadow request, are each refused by name when the scene is prepared on a device without ray queries, and on the portable recipe with ray queries enabled, and the refusal says which is missing. The frame reports what every request resolved to. Under `Traced` with nothing that reads the cascades, no cascade pass is recorded and the caster height map still is, and the air's shadow is unchanged to the byte.
items.ask: Is each request resolved from the registry's facts before anything is allocated, with no silent downgrade, and is the report the resolved value and not an echo of the request?

items.statement: On each device generation, every pipeline a traced scene uses is created before the scene is ready on that generation, in its day, night and capture variants, through the generation's creation authority, and none is created from then until the generation is lost or retired. A device replaced mid-run creates its own pipelines while it prepares, and none in the first frame it draws or after.

Every contribution that compiles the scene's shader draws under `Traced`: cooked placements read the traced operation, and a secondary view keeps its own cascade and the map method, with its bytes unchanged.

With the Sun's direct light out, a `Traced` frame of the valley equals the `Maps` frame of the same instant, at the tolerance the test states: the traced operation takes the place of the map lookup and nothing else.
items.ask: Is the stated tolerance no wider than rounding between two compilations of the same arithmetic, so that a traced shader that changed any other light term would fail?

items.statement: Paired rows on the valley's route are on record with the machine's load, for `Maps` and for `Traced` with and without lamp shadows: the whole frame and each pass by name, with the cascade passes' absence under `Traced` shown. Each tripwire of the design's cost account that the record trips has its investigation beside it. No figure in the record decides this item.
No exact baseline moves: with no request, every registered image on the Mac's two recipes and in Chrome is the one on main.

milestones.name: Sun shadows soften with distance from what casts them, and the Sun dims smoothly as it sets behind a ridge
milestones.quality_bar: Soft ray-traced Sun shadows as Cyberpunk 2077 and Shadow of the Tomb Raider ship them: sharp where a caster touches, wider with distance, with no grain at rest, a body that stays under its caster and no trail in motion at normal speed.

items.statement: A shadow's edge is sharp where its caster touches the receiver and widens with the caster's distance as the Sun's angular size sets it: at a prop's base, under a balloon, and from a ridge at a low Sun.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills of those three in the populated valley with the penumbra on and off, whole and as native-size crops across each edge.

items.statement: With the camera and the scene at rest, no penumbra shows grain, and none crawls from frame to frame.
items.inspect: Consecutive `realtime` frames at rest at the route's stops, as native-size crops of the widest penumbrae and as the difference between neighbouring frames.

items.statement: Along the route at normal speed, a moving caster's shadow stays under it in every frame: its body is never a frame behind. Where a shadow has moved off a still receiver, no remnant of it shows once the settle length and one more frame have passed. The evidence names the frame occlusion changed and states the settle length.
items.inspect: A `realtime` sequence of the route around a moving balloon's shadow and a named still receiver it crosses: the consecutive native-size frames from the one before occlusion changes there to two past the settle length, each numbered.

items.statement: Under a snap turn and across a camera cut, ground that comes into view settles without a flash or lasting grain.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences of a snap turn and a cut, as consecutive native-size frames around newly revealed ground.

items.statement: As the Sun sets behind a ridge, the Sun's light on a lit surface dims without a step.
items.inspect: A `fixed` time-lapse of the sunset at one stop, as consecutive frames and as the brightness of three lit points plotted against time.

items.statement: The history is committed only by a submitted frame, and is reset by a camera cut, a change of render extent and a device replacement: after each, no pixel reads a value from before it. A fragment with no matching history uses the centre ray in that frame, and so does a fragment whose settled history the centre ray contradicts. A fragment drawn after opaque geometry reads no history.
items.ask: Does the test plant a history value that a correct reset, and a correct override by the centre ray, must not return, so that a stale read fails?

items.statement: With the penumbra off the frame is M3's to the byte and the visibility pass is not recorded. Turning it off and on while the scene runs creates no pipeline and no resource.

Paired rows on the valley's route are on record with the machine's load, with the penumbra on and off: the whole frame, the forward pass with its inline centre rays, and the visibility pass's trace and filter by name. Each tripwire of the design's cost account that the record trips has its investigation beside it. No figure in the record decides this item.
No exact baseline moves: with no request, every registered image on the Mac's two recipes and in Chrome is the one on main.

milestones.name: Props and terrain are grounded: sky light is dimmed in creases and where things stand close together
milestones.quality_bar: Ray-traced ambient occlusion as Metro Exodus Enhanced Edition and Cyberpunk 2077 show it: contact darkening that belongs to the scene, with no halo at a silhouette, nothing that depends on what is on screen, and no trail at normal speed.

items.statement: The value multiplies the diffuse and the reflected sky light, with the material's own occlusion, and nothing else: with the Sun and lamps as the only light it changes no pixel.
In the populated valley in shade and after sunset, props, balloon baskets on the ground and creases of terrain are darker where they meet, and open ground is not darkened.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills at the route's stops in shade and at dusk with ambient occlusion on and off, whole and as native-size crops of contact points and of open ground.

items.statement: No dark or bright halo follows a silhouette, and turning the camera until an occluder leaves the view changes nothing on its receiver.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills before and after a turn that takes an occluder out of view, whole and as native-size crops at silhouettes and at the receiver.

items.statement: Occlusion shows no grain at rest. When an occluder moves away from a still receiver, once in view and once from off screen, the receiver's darkening is gone once the occlusion's settle length and one more frame have passed. The evidence names the frame the occluder moved and states the settle length.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences at rest and of an occluder leaving a named still receiver, in view and from off screen: the consecutive native-size frames from the one before it moves to two past the settle length, each numbered.

items.statement: No occlusion ray is longer than the radius the scene declares. Half extent and off are runtime values: off records no occlusion ray and restores M4's frame to the byte, and changing either while the scene runs creates no pipeline and no resource.

Paired rows on the valley's route are on record with the machine's load, with ambient occlusion off, at half extent and at full: the whole frame and the visibility pass by name. Each tripwire of the design's cost account that the record trips has its investigation beside it. No figure in the record decides this item.
No exact baseline moves: with no request, every registered image on the Mac's two recipes and in Chrome is the one on main.

milestones.name: The record says whether ray-traced Sun shadows cost no more than shadow maps on this Mac and are faster or better looking, and the Apple recipe selects them by default only if they are
milestones.quality_bar: A promotion record a reader can trust, as APPLE-TILE's integrated record is: paired, taken in one quiet sitting, each conclusion no stronger than its rows, and nothing claimed for a target that was not run. With every effect on, the valley is smooth at the display's full refresh or the record says why not.

items.statement: The design's twelve runs are retained from one sitting with other builders paused, on the final build, with frame GPU time and frame CPU time for every frame and, for every run, their medians, each pass by name, the load and the thermal state. Beside them are rows for `Traced` with hard edges, for lamp shadows and for ambient occlusion, which decide nothing, and the candidate's ten-minute run with the thermal state before and after. No figure in the record decides this item.
items.ask: Was the record taken in one sitting with other builders paused, on the final build, in the design's order, and do the retained frames give the medians it states?

items.statement: For each entry of the design's gain list (contact, distance, low Sun, softness), the record says whether the candidate's frame and the portable recipe's frame each pass it, from stills paired at the same stops and times on the final build, and every failure it names shows in the paired crops.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills of the portable recipe's frame and the candidate's at the route's stops at noon, at a low Sun and at dusk, whole and as native-size crops paired at contact points, beyond the cascades' reach, on low-Sun terrain and across soft edges.

items.statement: The record states, for each figure at each extent, the spread and whether the candidate was no higher or lower than the Apple tile recipe with `Maps`, and its conclusion: promoted, costs more or no gain. That conclusion is what the design's rule gives from the retained frames and M6.2's entries. The registry's qualified list holds this Mac's entry exactly when the conclusion is promoted, and the entry names the adapter, the Apple tile recipe and the configuration the sitting ran, penumbra included.
items.ask: Is the rule the script applies the design's, figure for figure and entry for entry, and does the list in the code match the conclusion?

items.statement: With a qualified entry present, an ordinary launch of the Mac window asks for `ray-query`, and `Auto` resolves to the entry's configuration, only when the adapter is the entry's and offers ray queries and the recipe is Apple tile. Outside any one of those, and with the list empty, the launch makes the device it makes today, `Auto` is `Maps`, and nothing is refused. On the portable recipe this Mac draws the map frame even when the launch names `ray-query`, and an explicit `Traced` there is refused by name, as is a launch that names `ray-query` on an adapter without it. An `Auto` scene whose traced preparation fails is ready as `Maps` and reports why.
items.ask: Is an ordinary launch on this Mac exercised through the host on both recipes, with the cases this Mac cannot show (another adapter, ray queries not offered, a traced preparation that fails) exercised through the registry's function and a forced failure?

items.statement: At the same stops and times, the candidate's frame differs from the portable recipe's only where the Sun's shadow differs: at shadow edges, at contact, and where maps gave no shadow or a coarse one. Sky, water, cloud, ground in full Sun and ground in full shade show no difference.
items.inspect: M6.2's paired stills with their difference images, amplified until a difference of one step shows, whole and as native-size crops of the largest differences and of sky, water, cloud, open sunlit ground and deep shade.

items.statement: ATTENDED SETUP: on the built-in display the capture-off release proving ground runs the valley's route on the Apple tile recipe with the traced Sun shadow, its penumbra, lamp shadows and ambient occlusion on, with an OS-reported presented interval for every submission. Each missed refresh is listed and investigated.
items.inspect: The presented-interval record of that run, with the list of missed refreshes and what each investigation found.

needs.what: Unlock the Mac, wake the built-in display and keep it awake for one sitting. The agent launches, records and reviews; nothing else is needed. Batch it with any other module's attended items.

items.statement: On the final build with every effect on together, the populated valley passes the lists of M3.2, M3.5, M4.2 to M4.6, M5.3, M5.4 and M5.5, and the effects agree: a surface in a traced shadow is not also lit by the Sun through the history, and occlusion does not darken a shadow's edge twice.
items.inspect: One capture pass on the final build: `fixed` stills at the route's stops at noon, at a low Sun, at dusk and at night, and `realtime` sequences of the route with the numbered frames M4.4 and M5.5 ask for, judged by those items' lists.

items.statement: The penumbra, the lamp-ray count, ambient occlusion and its extent, and the two settle lengths can each be listed and set by a caller that knows nothing of ray tracing, as the governor will, with its range and the history it invalidates declared. Setting each to both ends while the scene runs creates no pipeline and no resource.
items.ask: Does each quality value declare the history it invalidates, and does setting it invalidate that history and no other?

items.statement: A creator can turn each effect on in a scene from the public documentation: the launch request, the scene's requests, what each resolves to on a device without ray queries and on the portable recipe, when the Mac window asks for ray queries unasked, what each costs, and its limits.
items.ask: Could an agent that has read only the public documentation launch a scene with traced Sun shadows and ambient occlusion on this Mac, and say what the same scene does in Chrome?

items.statement: The maturity ledger has rows for the structure, traced shadows, soft shadows and ambient occlusion, with implementation, correctness, visuals and device kept apart, and claims nothing for a recipe or a target that was not run.
items.ask: Does each row match what M1 to M6 ran, with the physical iPhone recorded as owed?

items.statement: Every exact baseline holds after promotion, because the verifier's runs name no hardware feature.
